reference: Tamuka N, Mathonsi TE, Olwal TO, et al (2026) A Comparative Analysis of Self-Aware Reinforcement Learning Models for Real-Time Intrusion Detection in Fog Networks. Future Internet 18:100. https://doi.org/10.3390/fi18020100
setting_and_task: Per-flow binary intrusion response (allow / rate-limit / block) at fog nodes modelled as an online linear contextual bandit. Proposed HATS-RL: linear Thompson sampling with a composite monitor (EMA of regret proxy + EMA of feature-deviation 'uncertainty'), Page-Hinkley drift alarm that inflates posterior covariance (beta up to 2.0) and applies forgetting (gamma=0.02). F-HATS-RL adds randomized one-peer gossip of per-action sufficient statistics (A_a, b_a) with similarity-weighted convex merge. Compared with static threshold and LinUCB (Sec. 2.2, 3.3).
datasets_or_testbed: Custom Python 3.11 simulator: 8 fog nodes, synthetic 8-feature flows from multivariate normal benign distribution with random mean drift every 100 ticks, 15 attack types injected as mean shifts in bursts with overlap; 600 ticks (20,000 flows/node) per run; binary labels. Run on a single Dell Latitude laptop (Core i7, 1 TB SSD). No real traffic dataset (Sec. 3.1-3.4).
n_clients: 8 simulated fog nodes (Sec. 3.1).
partition_basis: Each node processes its own portion of generated traffic, described as heterogeneous (non-IID); exact per-node differences not specified (Sec. 3.1).
drift_type_and_cause: Gradual benign concept drift: small random drift added to the benign mean every 100 ticks; plus bursty, overlapping attack injections (attack onset probabilistic).
communication_topology: peer-to-peer: Every G (Tg = 10-50) ticks each node picks one peer uniformly at random and exchanges {A_a, b_a}; receiving node applies convex mixing with weight w_i in [0.1, 0.6] from exp(-d_i/0.5), where d_i is distance of node's running feature mean to the group mean (algorithm) or peer similarity d_ij (text). ~864 bytes per gossip (216 float32).
uncertainty_method: 'Uncertainty' U_t = L2 norm of EMA-standardized feature vector (feature-novelty score); Bayesian linear-regression posterior per action used for Thompson sampling. No predictive probability calibration.
uncertainty_as_control_signal: Yes: EMA of U_t combined with regret EMA (m_t = R_mean + c U_mean, c in [0.2,0.4]) feeds the Page-Hinkley drift alarm, which raises exploration and triggers forgetting
continual_mechanism: Drift-triggered adaptation of the online bandit model: covariance inflation (beta = min(2.0, beta+0.4)) and exponential forgetting of sufficient statistics (gamma = 0.02); continuous online updates.

Task: classification of driving behaviour/trajectory samples.
datasets_or_testbed: Joint dataset built from public NGSIM and HighD trajectories plus Brain4Cars behaviour labels; 20-step windows. Simulated MEC: 5 edge servers, links 10-50 Mbps, latency 10-100 ms; processes with sockets on one GPU server (Xeon Gold, 128 GB, RTX 3090) with LAN latency and bandwidth manually controlled. datasets_or_testbed: Prototype: 5 Huawei S5720 switches in two buildings, 5 servers (i7-8700, 16 GB RAM), VXLAN overlay with Open vSwitch and VMs; UEs are 3 Jetson AGX Xavier, 3 Jetson TX2, 3 Jetson Nano. n_clients: 9 physical UEs (Sec VI-A, Table II)
partition_basis: HARBox entries distributed over the 9 UEs proportionally to computing capability; each UE's data split into time slots with Poisson-distributed number and volume of datasets.

communication_topology: hierarchical: UEs -> base stations -> aggregators placed at base stations or cloudlets -> master aggregator (service). uncertainty_method: Uncertainty concerns network/training delays only (handled by contextual bandit with multiplicative weights). No predictive uncertainty of the model.

continual_mechanism: No model-level continual learning mechanism (no forgetting control, replay or regularisation). Fresh datasets are selected by minimum age subject to resource/delay constraints, and rounds repeat as data arrive.

summary: FLeeT is a Kubernetes-based FLaaS deployment toolkit in which federation roles and topology are declared in YAML, evaluated on FEMNIST and CIFAR-10 with Docker-simulated clients and five Raspberry Pi 5 edge clients in a single aggregator-client layout, reporting per-session time, CPU, memory and traffic but no repeats, baselines, drift or uncertainty.
